findings.body: The volume mount references `./deploy/mongo/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py`, but I could not confirm this file exists at the reviewed commit — my earlier attempt to list `deploy/mongo/` returned no entries. If the file is absent, Docker will create a directory at `/usr/local/bin/kernel-bypass-entrypoint.py` instead of mounting the script, and `python3` will fail trying to execute a directory, producing a confusing error for anyone running the documented `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.kernel-bypass.yml up -d`. I am requesting a read of the script path to confirm or deny.
findings.title: Verify the entrypoint script exists before relying on the volume mount

lookups.why: Verify that 'mongod' and 'mongo-secrets' are the correct service names in the base compose file, and check what image mongo-secrets uses to determine if it also needs the entrypoint shim.
Verify the entrypoint script exists at the reviewed commit and check whether it correctly handles extra command arguments passed through from the base compose service.

value.summary: The kernel-bypass overlay is syntactically correct and the approach (GLIBC_TUNABLES + entrypoint shim) is sound, but I need to verify the referenced entrypoint script exists in the tree and that the service names match the base compose file before giving a final verdict.
